groningen-narrative-authority-winter-sch.about:
The Netherlands Winter School on Narrative, hosted by the University of Groningen, runs 18–22 January 2027 on the theme 'Narrative and Authority'. Lectures and workshops draw on psychology, literary and cultural studies and cognitive science, ending with a symposium, 'Authors of the Story Economy'.

It is for master's and PhD students, early-career researchers and professionals interested in storytelling. Everyone gets a certificate; completing an extra assignment gives a 140-hour workload statement (5 ECTS).

Fees are modest and include lunches and a dinner; a dormitory option is available. Apply with a CV and one-page motivation letter by 15 November 2026.
highlights: Interdisciplinary: psychology, literature, cognitive science
Up to 5 ECTS
Housing option included in fee
groningen-narrative-authority-winter-sch.eligibility: Master's and PhD students, early-career researchers and professionals; English sufficient for discussion and presentation.
how_to_apply: Prepare a CV and one-page motivation letter.
Submit the online application form by 15 November 2026.
Pay the fee after acceptance.
groningen-narrative-authority-winter-sch.costs: Regular €425 (no housing) or €500 (with dormitory 17–22 Jan); affiliated organisations €325/€400; Groningen students/staff €150. Includes weekday lunches, drinks and a dinner.

gsumun-2026.about:
GSUMUN is Georgia State University's annual Model UN conference in downtown Atlanta, run by its Model UN programme.

The conference runs 11–12 November 2026 at Georgia State University, Atlanta, United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Use 'Register Now' on the official site before registration closes on 2 Nov 2026 (23:59). The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 11–12 November 2026 in Atlanta, United States
Last-minute option: registration closes 2 Nov 2026
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
gsumun-2026.eligibility: Open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Use 'Register Now' on the official site before registration closes on 2 Nov 2026 (23:59).
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
gsumun-2026.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

haarlem-mun-2027.about:
HMUN is a Dutch school conference in Haarlem, close to Amsterdam, welcoming delegates, student officers, MUN directors and guest speakers; its site lists committees plus hotel and restaurant tips for visiting schools.

The conference runs 2–4 April 2027 at venues in Haarlem, Netherlands. It is open to secondary school students, student officers and MUN directors with school delegations. Working language: English.

Applications are open on the 'Applications' page of the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

Applications open now; near Amsterdam
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page

hague-academy-international-law-summer-c.about:
The Hague Academy of International Law, founded in 1923 and housed in the Peace Palace (seat of the International Court of Justice), runs its annual Summer Courses in two three-week sessions: Public International Law, 5–23 July 2027, and Private International Law, 26 July – 13 August 2027. Leading judges, diplomats and professors give lectures in English and French, and participants can also apply for Directed Studies seminars.

The courses are designed for students and practitioners with a prior grounding in international law; participants come from all over the world. Online attendance is also possible (no scholarships for online).

Registration opens on 1 November each year. Scholarship applicants need an enrolment or employment proof, diploma, CV, motivation letter and a recommendation letter from an international-law professor; results are sent in April.
highlights: Lectures at the Peace Palace
Scholarships for students and young professionals
Public or private international law sessions
hague-academy-international-law-summer-c.eligibility: Students (typically law, advanced bachelor's and above) and practitioners with prior grounding in international law; any nationality; English or French.
how_to_apply: Read the conditions for admission and application guidelines.
Register online from 1 November 2026 (full-fee or scholarship route).
Scholarship applicants: upload passport, photo, proof of enrolment/employment, diploma, CV and motivation letter; ask an international-law professor to email a recommendation.
Wait for results (scholarships: April 2027).
hague-academy-international-law-summer-c.costs: Registration fee on the full-fee page; scholarships available for in-person attendance (not online). Travel and accommodation extra unless covered by a scholarship.

han-online-open-day-2026-11.about:
HAN University of Applied Sciences (Arnhem and Nijmegen) runs an Online Open Day for prospective international students. On Saturday 14 November 2026 (10:00–17:15 CET), staff and students of its English-taught Bachelor's and Master's programmes host live info sessions and chats, from International Business and Engineering to International Social Work.

Recorded talk shows on visas, housing, admission, scholarships and student life are available to watch beforehand. It is a practical way to compare Dutch applied-science programmes before applying via Studielink.
highlights: Live programme sessions and chats
Practical talks on visas, housing, scholarships
Free, join from home
han-online-open-day-2026-11.eligibility: Prospective international Bachelor's and Master's students from any country.
how_to_apply: Open the Online Open Day page and pre-register
Pick the programme sessions you want
Watch the recorded talk shows on visas and housing
Join live on 14 Nov 2026

hanyang-international-summer-school-2027.about:
Hanyang International Summer School (HISS) is one of Korea's larger summer programmes, held at Hanyang University in central Seoul. It offers English-taught academic courses across disciplines, Korean language classes and a cultural and field-trip programme for international university students.

The 2027 programme details will be published in mid-December 2026 (a tentative preview is already online) and applications open on 1 January 2027.

Hanyang usually offers partner-university and early-bird discounts; check the tuition page when the 2027 cycle opens.
highlights: English-taught courses in central Seoul
Korean language and K-culture activities
Applications open 1 January 2027
hanyang-international-summer-school-2027.eligibility: University students worldwide (see the HISS site for 2027 requirements).
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 programme when it is published in mid-December 2026.
Apply online from 1 January 2027.
Pay tuition by the stated deadline.
Apply for a visa if required.
hanyang-international-summer-school-2027.costs: 2027 fees to be published; contact summerschool@hanyang.ac.kr.

hanyang-international-winter-school-2026.about:
Hanyang International Winter School (HIWS) runs short English-taught sessions in Seoul for international university students. Session A runs 26 December 2026 – 8 January 2027 and Session B 19 January – 3 February 2027; you can take one or both. Courses are listed on each session's Courses page, alongside cultural activities around Seoul.

One session costs KRW 1,600,000–1,700,000 plus a KRW 100,000 application fee; partner-university students get KRW 200,000 off. A Hanyang Ambassador Scholarship covers 100% of tuition for one student per session.

Payment deadlines: 22 November 2026 for Session A, 27 December 2026 for Session B.
highlights: Two short sessions over the winter break
Full-tuition Ambassador Scholarship (one per session)
English-taught courses in central Seoul
hanyang-international-winter-school-2026.eligibility: Current university students worldwide (check the Apply/FAQ pages for exact requirements).
how_to_apply: Choose Session A, B or both.
Apply online via the HIWS application page.
Pay the application fee and tuition by 22 Nov (A) or 27 Dec 2026 (B).
Optionally apply for the Ambassador Scholarship (Session B until 13 Nov 2026).
hanyang-international-winter-school-2026.costs: Application KRW 100,000; one session KRW 1,600,000 (partner) or KRW 1,700,000 (regular); both sessions KRW 2,600,000–2,700,000. Ambassador Scholarship = 100% tuition for one student per session. Meals, transport and materials extra.

harvard-debate-council-summer-workshops-.about:
The Harvard Debate Council Summer Workshops (HDCSW) are among the largest high-school debate camps in the world. Students choose a track (World Schools, Public Forum, Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Congressional Debate, competitive speech or communication skills) and train daily with experienced coaches, finishing with practice tournaments.

The workshops run each July: in 2026 Session One ran 28 June–10 July (in person and online) and Session Two 12–24 July, with four-week policy options; almost 700 students attended, including students from 20 countries. Registration for the next summer opens on 1 December. They welcome students from around the world and every experience level, from beginners to national-championship competitors.
highlights: Large international cohort on Harvard's campus
Tracks for World Schools, Public Forum, Policy and more
Online tracks for students who cannot travel
harvard-debate-council-summer-workshops-.eligibility: High-school students of any experience level from any country.
how_to_apply: Check 2027 sessions and tracks on hdcsw.org
Register online from 1 December 2026
Choose in-person (residential) or online
Pay tuition and arrange a US visa for in-person sessions
harvard-debate-council-summer-workshops-.costs: Paid; tuition and residential fees published on the HDCSW site with registration.

heidelberg-international-summer-school-g.about:
Heidelberg University's International Summer School for German Language and Culture runs 31 July – 26 August 2027 in the historic university town of Heidelberg. Course I offers German from beginner (A1) to advanced (C1) level with a focus on speaking; Course II is a further-training course for teachers of German and postgraduate German students; Course III is Business German.

Classes have about 14–20 participants, and passing a written exam earns an additional diploma worth 4 ECTS. A cultural programme rounds off the course.

Registration opens on 15 January 2027 via the form on the official page.
highlights: Germany's oldest university
All levels A1–C1 plus Business German
4-ECTS diploma option
heidelberg-international-summer-school-g.eligibility: Adults and students worldwide interested in German; place by level. Course II is for German teachers and postgraduate German students.
how_to_apply: Check the course options and fees on the official page.
Register from 15 January 2027 using the online form.
Pay the fee to confirm your place.
Arrange a visa and accommodation if needed.
heidelberg-international-summer-school-g.costs: Fees on the official 'Registration & Fee' section.

hkust-international-summer-campus-summer.about:
The HKUST International Summer Campus brings international students to the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology's Clear Water Bay campus from June to August 2027. The Summer School track offers undergraduate-level, credit-bearing courses taught by HKUST faculty, for 4 or 8 weeks.

A separate 8-week Summer Undergraduate Research track places students in HKUST labs (listed separately on Meridian).

Application dates, fees and eligibility are published on the summer campus site; contact summer.school@ust.hk for details.
highlights: Courses taught by HKUST faculty
4- or 8-week options
Credit-bearing
hkust-international-summer-campus-summer.eligibility: Undergraduate students (see the official application page for detailed requirements).
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 course list on the summer campus site.
Apply through the HKUST Summer School application page.
Pay fees after admission and arrange a Hong Kong entry permit if needed.
hkust-international-summer-campus-summer.costs: Fees to be published on the HKUST summer campus site.

hokkaido-summer-institute-2027.about:
Since 2016 Hokkaido University has run the Hokkaido Summer Institute (HSI), bringing world-leading researchers to Sapporo to teach short courses with HU faculty. Around 150 English-taught courses run between June and October, attended by 750+ students from overseas universities and 1,500 HU students, in fields from marine biology, veterinary medicine and Antarctic science to tourism, gender studies, sustainability and Japanese culture, many with field training.

University and graduate students enrolled as degree students can take courses for 1 or 2 credits. Tuition for students is just JPY 14,800 per 1-credit course (JPY 29,600 for 2 credits), plus a JPY 1,500 system fee, though some field courses add accommodation and travel costs. HSI offers no scholarships of its own.
highlights: ~150 English-taught courses with international researchers
Field schools across Hokkaido
Very affordable tuition for students (JPY 14,800 per credit-course)
hokkaido-summer-institute-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled as degree students at a university or graduate school at the time of application and during the course; working adults can join non-credit professional courses. All nationalities.
how_to_apply: Check the HSI site from late January 2027 for courses and application windows
Create an account, choose courses and upload documents in an application window
Pay the JPY 1,500 system usage fee by credit card
After acceptance, pay tuition, book accommodation and arrange insurance/visa
hokkaido-summer-institute-2027.costs: Students: JPY 14,800 (1-credit) or JPY 29,600 (2-credit) tuition per course plus JPY 1,500 system fee (2025/26 rates); some field courses have extra costs. No HSI scholarships.

hsg-online-bachelors-open-day-2026-11.about:
The University of St.Gallen (HSG) is one of Europe's leading business and economics universities. Its online open days, held on Zoom, are for prospective students anywhere in the world who cannot attend an on-campus open day.

The event starts with an overview of the Bachelor's programmes, followed by current students sharing their experience of student life and campus culture, a general Q&A, and live sessions for individual programmes where you can ask about admission requirements. A relaxed 'Coffee-to-grow Student Talk' lets you chat with students in small groups. Registration through the official form is required; you choose the programmes you are interested in when you sign up.

Programme presentations cover Business Administration, Economics, International Affairs, Law and Computer Science (some taught in German, with English tracks in Economics and International Affairs).
highlights: Designed for students who cannot visit campus
English-taught Economics and International Affairs tracks
Free, live on Zoom
hsg-online-bachelors-open-day-2026-11.eligibility: Secondary-school students and others considering a Bachelor's at HSG, from any country.
how_to_apply: Open the event page and register
Choose the programme presentations you want
Get Zoom links by email
Join on 27 Nov 2026

huwisu-summer-2027.about:
HUWISU (Humboldt-Universität International Summer University) brings international students to one of Germany's most famous universities in central Berlin. Session 1 begins 14 June 2027 and Session 2 on 12 July 2027. Courses use hands-on methods in fields such as metropolitan research and urban planning, law and economics, and German literature, plus German language; some courses can be combined.

A free extracurricular programme explores Berlin's life, history and culture. The full 2027 course programme is published in December 2026.

The one-off programme fee is €160 plus course fees listed per course, with €50 discounts for returning participants, partner-university students and those taking more than one course.
highlights: Courses in the heart of Berlin
Free cultural programme
Combine two courses with a discount
huwisu-summer-2027.eligibility: University students and graduates worldwide; English (or German for German-taught courses). See the HUWISU application page.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 course list (published December 2026).
Apply online via the HUWISU application page.
Pay the €160 programme fee and course fee.
Look for external funding (DAAD, Santander) early.

iaac-astronomy-astrophysics-competition-.about:
IAAC is an educational science competition open to students from all countries in three age groups (Junior: grade 10 and below; Youth: grades 11–13; Senior: university). The free Qualification Round has five astronomy problems solved at home and submitted online; qualifiers take a Pre-Final exam based on a real research paper, and the best sit a supervised online Final with around 30 questions.

Top performers receive prizes worth about USD 2,500, including cash and telescopes signed by astronaut Frank De Winne and Nobel laureates; there are also national awards and certificates for all participants. The 2027 edition follows the annual cycle (qualification in spring, final in early summer).
highlights: Free qualification round, open to all countries
Prizes incl. telescopes signed by Nobel laureates
Certificates for every participant
iaac-astronomy-astrophysics-competition-.eligibility: Current high-school and university students of any grade and country. Good English helps (some problems use research material).
how_to_apply: Check iaac.space for the 2027 Qualification Round problems
Solve the five problems and submit online before the deadline
If you qualify, register for the Pre-Final (small fee, aid available)
Take the online Final if selected
iaac-astronomy-astrophysics-competition-.costs: Qualification Round free; Pre-Final registration about EUR 13 (full and partial waivers available).

iac-austin-mun-2027.about:
International Academic Competitions (IAC), the organiser of the National History Bee and Geography Bee, runs one-day Model UN regional conferences for younger students. Students compete individually (no school group needed) in standard committees on a set topic, with separate awards for each grade; country assignments are made about two weeks before the event.

The conference runs 1 May 2027 at Cedar Park Recreation Center, United States. It is open to students in grades 4–8 (individually or with a school group). Working language: English.

Register on IAC's regionals registration page by 2027-04-16; payment is due at least a week before the conference. Fees: one committee $85, both committees $125 (online payments carry a 5% processing fee). As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

Beginner-friendly: no prior qualification or school team needed
Fees: one committee $85, both committees $125 (online payments carry a 5% processing fee)

iac-model-un-national-championships-2027.about:
The IAC Model UN National Championships bring together younger delegates who earned an award at any regional Model UN conference during the 2026–27 school year. Students compete solo in preliminary committees, followed by playoffs, alongside IAC's other middle- and elementary-school national championships.

The conference runs 28–31 May 2027 at Hyatt Regency Orlando (with the IAC Middle & Elementary School National Championships), United States. It is open to students in grades 4–8 who won any award at a regional Model UN conference (IAC or not) or in Intro to Model UN during 2026–27. Working language: English.

Qualify by winning an award at any 2026–27 regional MUN, then register on the IAC site by the initial deadline of 11 May 2027. Fee: $115 per student per preliminary committee; playoffs at no extra cost. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

icehacks-2026.about:
IceHacks 2026 is a fully virtual hackathon hosted by CodeStarters, a student-led nonprofit that makes computer-science and AI education more accessible. Participants turn an idea into a working project (software, hardware or something in between) during the hacking week of 8–15 November 2026, then submit it for judging.

It is free, beginner-friendly and run through Devpost and Discord. There are no cash prizes; rewards are sponsor credits, subscriptions, scholarships and other non-cash prizes.
highlights: First-hackathon friendly
Software, hardware or AI projects
Free, fully online
icehacks-2026.eligibility: High-school students (and other student builders) from anywhere; check Devpost rules for age limits.

Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

igrayuchi-russian-summer-school-bishkek-.about:
Igrayuchi's Central Asia summer school combines two weeks in Bishkek (Kyrgyzstan) and two weeks in Almaty (Kazakhstan) between 21 June and 18 July 2027. Participants learn Russian in two Russian-speaking capitals while exploring Soviet architecture, nomadic culture, Lake Issyk-Kul and the Tien Shan mountains.

Classes are 20 academic hours per week (Monday-Friday) in small groups with native-speaker teachers, with all materials included, plus films, games, city walks, culinary and craft workshops and one guided trip outside the city each week. The school helps with accommodation and extra travel; many nationalities (EU, UK, USA, Japan, South Korea and others) need no visa.

Fees: a non-refundable registration fee of EUR 80 (1-2 weeks) or EUR 100 (3-4 weeks) plus tuition of EUR 235-250 per week depending on length. Accommodation, flights and meals are extra.
highlights: Two countries in one programme
Trips to Lake Issyk-Kul and the Tien Shan
20 academic hours of Russian per week
igrayuchi-russian-summer-school-bishkek-.eligibility: Adult learners of Russian of any nationality; levels placed by the school.
how_to_apply: Open the Bishkek + Almaty page on igrayuchi.com.
Choose your weeks between 21 June and 18 July 2027.
Submit the booking form and pay the registration fee.
Pay tuition, arrange accommodation and travel.
igrayuchi-russian-summer-school-bishkek-.costs: Registration EUR 80 (1-2 weeks) or EUR 100 (3-4 weeks); tuition EUR 235-250 per week. Accommodation, flights, meals and the Bishkek-Almaty transfer arrangements as advised by the school.

igrayuchi-russian-winter-school-yerevan-.about:
Igrayuchi, a Russian-as-a-foreign-language project founded by linguist Oleg Ilyasov, runs a winter school in Yerevan from 25 January to 21 February 2027. Learners improve their Russian in a Russian-speaking, multicultural city while discovering Armenian history, monasteries, food and wine culture.

Classes are 20 academic hours per week (Monday-Friday) in small groups with native-speaker teachers, with all materials included, plus films, games, city walks, culinary and craft workshops and one guided trip outside the city each week. The school helps with accommodation and extra travel; many nationalities (EU, UK, USA, Japan, South Korea and others) need no visa.

Fees: a non-refundable registration fee of EUR 80 (1-2 weeks) or EUR 100 (3-4 weeks) plus tuition of EUR 235-250 per week depending on length. Accommodation, flights and meals are extra.
highlights: Join for 1 to 4 weeks
20 academic hours a week plus a weekly trip (e.g. Lake Sevan)
Affordable from about EUR 330 for one week
igrayuchi-russian-winter-school-yerevan-.eligibility: Adult learners of Russian of any nationality; levels placed by the school.
how_to_apply: Open the Yerevan school page on igrayuchi.com.
Choose how many weeks you want (25 Jan - 21 Feb 2027).
Submit the booking form and pay the registration fee.
Pay tuition, arrange accommodation (the school can help) and travel to Yerevan.
igrayuchi-russian-winter-school-yerevan-.costs: Registration EUR 80 (1-2 weeks) or EUR 100 (3-4 weeks), non-refundable; tuition EUR 250/week (1 week) down to EUR 235/week (4 weeks). Accommodation, flights and meals extra.

imperial-postgraduate-virtual-open-days-.about:
Imperial College London, one of the world's top science, engineering, medicine and business universities, hosts virtual open days for individual postgraduate programmes. In November 2026 sessions include, for example, the online Health Policy programme, the MRes in Translational Research in Surgery, the MRes in Medical Robotics and Image-Guided Intervention and the MSc in Human Molecular Genetics, among many others.

Each session lasts about an hour on a fixed date (mostly midday UK time) and has its own free registration. They are the best way to ask course leaders about entry requirements, research projects and funding before applying.
highlights: Programme-specific sessions with course leaders
Many dates through November 2026
Free; register per session
imperial-postgraduate-virtual-open-days-.eligibility: Prospective postgraduate students from any country.
how_to_apply: Open Imperial's Postgraduate Virtual Open Day page
Find the programme you are interested in
Register for its session
Join online at the scheduled time

insead-summer-school-2027.about:
INSEAD, one of the world's leading business schools, runs a two-week full-time summer school on its Europe campus in Fontainebleau near Paris. The curriculum covers business foundations, leadership, applied entrepreneurship and AI-enabled venture creation, taught through case discussions, team projects, simulations and company visits.

It is for 18–24-year-olds who have finished high school: students preparing for, studying for or recently finished a bachelor's degree, in any subject. The 2026 class had 114 participants from 30 nationalities. Completion earns 5 ECTS.

The 2027 edition runs 26 July – 6 August 2027 and applications are open until 31 May 2027.
highlights: Taught by INSEAD faculty on the Fontainebleau campus
5 ECTS credits
Around 30 nationalities per cohort
insead-summer-school-2027.eligibility: Ages 18–24 who have completed high school (pre-university, current or recent bachelor's students); any nationality and major; strong English.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page.
Complete the online application form.
Submit before 31 May 2027 (one intake per year).
Pay the fee after admission.
insead-summer-school-2027.costs: Tuition €5,975; travel and accommodation not included. No scholarships listed; reduced rate for family of INSEAD alumni.

interlochen-arts-camp-2027.about:
Interlochen Arts Camp is a residential summer arts camp on a large lakeside campus in northern Michigan. Young artists train intensively in their chosen discipline (orchestra, band, piano, voice, dance, theatre, musical theatre, visual arts, creative writing, film and more) with professional faculty, perform or exhibit, and live alongside campers from across the US and around the world.

Camp 2027 offers one-week intensives for grades 9–12 (19–25 June), two-, three-, four- and six-week camps between 27 June and 8 August for grades 3–12. Applications for 2027 are already open; many programmes require an audition or portfolio, and places fill quickly. Interlochen welcomes international students (campers from about 50 countries each year) and offers a dedicated page of guidance for international families.
highlights: Professional-level training in music, dance, theatre, visual arts, writing and film
Students from around 50 countries
Substantial need- and merit-based financial aid
interlochen-arts-camp-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 3–12 (age group by current grade) from any country. Some programmes require an audition or portfolio. International students need a US visa.
how_to_apply: Choose a programme and session for summer 2027 on the camp website
Create an account and complete the online application
Upload audition recordings or portfolio if your programme requires it
Apply for financial aid at the same time
Apply early: programmes fill on a rolling basis
interlochen-arts-camp-2027.costs: Paid residential camp; tuition depends on session length and is listed on Interlochen's tuition and financial-aid pages. Interlochen reports that 86% of campers receive financial aid (need- and merit-based).

international-youth-math-challenge-2027.about:
The International Youth Math Challenge is an educational mathematics competition open to current high-school and university students from all grades and countries. The free Qualification Round (September) has five problems of varying difficulty; depending on your age group you need to solve three or four to advance.

The Pre-Final Round (November) is a 60-minute exam that includes reading a real research paper (small registration fee, financial aid available), and finalists take a supervised online exam in December. Winners receive certificates and prizes worth over USD 1,400, and there are awards for teachers and schools. The 2026 qualification has closed; the next entry point is the 2027 Qualification Round.
highlights: Free first round, open to every country
Problems from geometry to number theory
Certificates for all; prizes over USD 1,400
international-youth-math-challenge-2027.eligibility: Current high-school and university students of any grade and country; English fluency helps.
how_to_apply: Check iymc.info for the 2027 Qualification Round problems
Solve the problems and submit online before the September deadline
Register for the Pre-Final if you qualify
Take the supervised online Final in December
international-youth-math-challenge-2027.costs: Qualification Round free; Pre-Final registration about EUR 13 (financial aid available).

international-zhautykov-olympiad-2027.about:
The International Zhautykov Olympiad (IZhO) is a long-running international olympiad in mathematics, physics and computer science for secondary-school students, organised by Kazakhstan's Daryn centre at the Republican Physics and Mathematics School (Fizmat) in Almaty. The 2026 edition (10-15 January) gathered over 700 students from about 15 countries, including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Türkiye. The 23rd edition is expected in January 2027.

Each team has up to 3 mathematics, 2 physics and 2 computer-science contestants plus leaders; problems can be solved in the student's own language. Up to four teams per foreign country may take part, and teams are registered through the ministry of education or the body responsible for national olympiad teams. Medals and team rankings are awarded, and the olympiad is a strong stepping stone towards IMO, IPhO and IOI selection.
highlights: Maths, physics and informatics team olympiad with 700+ students
Food and accommodation in Almaty covered by organisers
Georgia regularly sends teams
international-zhautykov-olympiad-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students strong in maths, physics or informatics, selected by their country's national olympiad body. Foreign teams must be registered through the ministry of education or the organisation that manages national olympiad teams (in Georgia, ask your olympiad coordinator or the Ministry/National Assessment and Examinations Center).
how_to_apply: Do well in your national olympiad in maths, physics or informatics.
Ask your national olympiad coordinator or ministry whether your country will send an IZhO 2027 team.
The ministry pre-registers the team (2026 pattern: by mid-November) and confirms the full team (by mid-December).
Travel to Almaty in January with your team leader.
international-zhautykov-olympiad-2027.costs: Participation fee charged per participant and leader (USD 100 in recent invitations); organisers cover food and accommodation in Almaty; travel is paid by the sending country or school.

ipd-baku-summer-academy-2027.about:
The Institute for Peace and Dialogue (IPD), based in Basel, runs a School of Conflict Management, Cross-Cultural Communication, Leadership, Mediation and Human Resources Management. Its Baku Summer Academy takes place on 1-7 July 2027 at the Ganjali Plaza Hotel in Baku and combines interactive non-formal training with a sightseeing trip to Astara on the Iranian border (4 July).

It suits university students, graduates and young professionals in international relations, peace studies, law or NGO work who want a short international certificate course in the South Caucasus. Azerbaijan offers e-visas to many nationalities, and the organisers provide invitation letters where needed.
highlights: Training in mediation, leadership and cross-cultural communication
Held in central Baku with a day trip to Astara
Discounts of 10% for students, groups and alumni
ipd-baku-summer-academy-2027.eligibility: Students, graduates and young professionals of any nationality (adults). Applicants submit education and work history and a motivation statement (max 500 words).
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 application form from the IPD Trainings & Events page.
Complete personal details, education, experience and a motivation letter.
Choose a fee option and send the form before 25 March 2027 (early bird) or 31 May 2027 (late).
Pay the participation fee and apply for an Azerbaijani e-visa if needed.
ipd-baku-summer-academy-2027.costs: Early bird: EUR 1,550 (no accommodation), EUR 1,750 (double room) or EUR 2,150 (single room). Late: EUR 1,950 / 2,050 / 2,550. 10% discounts for students, small NGOs, groups and alumni. Cancellation charges from EUR 550 apply after applying.

issai-nu-summer-research-program-2027.about:
Since 2021 ISSAI, the Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence at Nazarbayev University in Astana, has run a Summer Research Program for talented students from Kazakhstan and around the world. High school students follow a five-to-six-week track (a week of masterclasses on language models, computer vision and generative AI, then supervised project work), while university students join a longer research track of up to nine weeks.

In 2026 ISSAI received over 1,200 applications and selected 77 participants, including high school students from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia and university students from Kazakhstan and Europe. Tracks included AI avatars, audio-visual models and speech recognition, AI agents, mobile apps, software engineering and robotics, ending with public project presentations.
highlights: Real AI research with ISSAI scientists
Open to international high school and university students
Very selective: 77 places from 1,200+ applicants in 2026
issai-nu-summer-research-program-2027.eligibility: High school and university students with programming and maths skills, from Kazakhstan or abroad. Check the 2027 call for age limits, accommodation and travel arrangements.
how_to_apply: Watch issai.nu.edu.kz (SRP menu) for the 2027 call, expected in early 2027.
Prepare a CV, transcripts and evidence of coding/AI projects.
Submit the online application before the deadline.
If selected, travel to Astana for June-July 2027.
issai-nu-summer-research-program-2027.costs: No tuition fee has been mentioned in past calls; travel and living costs for international participants should be confirmed in the 2027 call.

jugendwettbewerb-informatik-2027.about:
The Jugendwettbewerb Informatik is aimed at young people with little or no programming experience. Rounds 1 and 2 are online with three levels (bronze, silver, gold), and each starts with a practice contest; round 3 is a take-home round using your own programming tools. Individuals or teams (up to two in rounds 1–2, up to four in round 3) can take part.

It leads naturally into the Bundeswettbewerb Informatik and Germany's IOI selection.
highlights: Beginner friendly; three levels
Online rounds with practice contests
Free
jugendwettbewerb-informatik-2027.eligibility: Students recommended from grade 5 (possible from grade 3) at schools in Germany and German schools abroad.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to register the class on bwinf.de
Try the practice contest
Take rounds 1 and 2 online in spring 2027

kaggle-enveda-casmi-2026.about:
The Critical Assessment of Small Molecule Identification (CASMI) 2026, run with Enveda on Kaggle, challenges participants to build models that predict 2D chemical structures of small molecules from tandem mass spectra of complex biological extracts, helping map the chemical diversity of nature.

It started on 14 September 2026; accept the rules by 7 December and submit by 14 December 2026. Prizes total USD 50,000 (USD 16,000 for first place). Ideal for chemistry, bioinformatics and ML students.
highlights: USD 50,000 prize pool
Free, solo or in teams on Kaggle
Public leaderboard and notebooks to learn from
kaggle-enveda-casmi-2026.eligibility: Open to Kaggle users worldwide who meet the competition rules (normally 18+ or the age of majority, or younger with parental consent where the rules allow); residents of countries under US sanctions are excluded. Read the Rules tab before joining.
how_to_apply: Create a free Kaggle account and verify your phone
Open the competition page and accept the rules before the entry deadline
Download the data / use Kaggle notebooks
Submit predictions or your write-up before the final deadline

kaggle-gemma-4-developer-agent-2026.about:
In this featured Kaggle competition, Google asks participants to post-train an open Gemma 4 model into a reliable autonomous agent that navigates complex codebases and drafts fixes for real software issues, while running offline on consumer hardware.

It started on 23 September 2026. An optional research-paper track closes on 12 November 2026; accept the rules by 25 November and make final submissions by 2 December 2026. Total prizes across both tracks: USD 110,000.

kaggle-google-quantum-circuit-compilatio.about:
Google Quantum AI's featured Kaggle competition asks participants to compile quantum circuits more efficiently while keeping results verifiable, reducing the resources quantum applications need. It started on 22 October 2026, with a mid-competition milestone prize on 20 November 2026.

Teams must accept the rules by 13 January 2027 and make final submissions by 20 January 2027. Prizes total USD 150,000 (USD 50,000 for first place plus milestone, longest-leader and task prizes). A good fit for university students in physics, maths or computer science.

kaggle-name-that-llm-2027.about:
Name That LLM is a featured Kaggle code competition on AI provenance: given short unlabeled passages, participants build models that identify which of 18 leading language models wrote each one. Submissions are scored on balanced accuracy, and the work feeds research on auditing and attributing AI-generated text.

The competition started on 14 October 2026; accept the rules by 6 January 2027 and submit by 13 January 2027. Prize pool USD 50,000.

kaggle-nfl-big-data-bowl-2027.about:
The NFL Big Data Bowl is the National Football League's annual analytics hackathon on Kaggle. For 2027, entrants build an analytical framework that links 10 Hz Combine sensor-tracking data to regular-season performance, helping scouts find hidden talent and design player-development plans. Submissions are written notebooks (max. 2,000 words, fewer than 10 figures).

It runs from 6 October 2026; final submissions are due 6 January 2027, judging runs to 25 January and results are expected on 26 January 2027. Prize pool USD 100,000; past finalists have been invited to present at the NFL Scouting Combine. A great portfolio piece for statistics and data-science students.

Free, solo or in teams on Kaggle
Public leaderboard and notebooks to learn from

kaggle-pokemon-tcg-ai-battle-playground-.about:
This Kaggle 'Playground' simulation competition continues the featured Pokémon TCG AI Battle Challenge. Participants design, train and test AI agents that play the Pokémon Trading Card Game in a best-of-three format, where probability, hidden information and strategic planning decide matches. Agents play each other continuously on a live leaderboard.

It runs from 29 September 2026; accept the rules by 1 January 2027 and submit by 8 January 2027. Games continue for two weeks after the deadline, then a Bradley-Terry tournament sets the final standings. The top five teams win Kaggle merchandise. A friendly entry point to game-playing AI for students.

Great intro to reinforcement learning and game AI
Free; Kaggle merchandise for top 5

Accept the competition rules before 1 Jan 2027
Build an agent with the starter notebook
Submit agents before 8 Jan 2027 and watch the leaderboard

kaggle-squares-in-squares-2027.about:
Squares in Squares is a Kaggle playground competition on a classic open problem in combinatorial geometry: pack n non-overlapping unit squares into the smallest axis-aligned square, across 1,000 puzzles. Many optimal packings are still unknown, so strong algorithms can genuinely improve the state of the art.

It runs from 21 October 2026 to 18 July 2027, with milestone prizes for the leaderboard leader on 17 January and 18 April 2027. The long timeline and puzzle-like format make it accessible to strong school and university maths/programming students.
highlights: USD 50,000 prize pool incl. milestone prizes
Free, solo or in teams on Kaggle
Public leaderboard and notebooks to learn from

kenyon-review-young-writers-summer-2027.about:
The Kenyon Review Young Writers Summer Workshops bring high-school writers to Kenyon College in Gambier, Ohio, home of The Kenyon Review. In multi-genre workshops led by published poets and fiction writers, students write every day, give and receive feedback, attend readings and finish with a public reading of their work.

2027 residential sessions run 27 June–10 July and 18–31 July (applications due 1 March 2027); a one-week online multi-genre workshop runs 20–26 June (applications open March 2027). The programme welcomes talented high-school students from around the world.
highlights: Daily writing workshops with published authors
Two residential sessions on the Kenyon College campus
One-week online alternative
kenyon-review-young-writers-summer-2027.eligibility: High-school students from any country who write in English.
how_to_apply: Prepare a writing sample
Apply online by 1 March 2027 for the residential sessions (online session applications open March 2027)
Request financial aid if needed
Arrange travel and a US visa for the residential programme
kenyon-review-young-writers-summer-2027.costs: Paid; tuition, room and board listed on the Kenyon Review Young Writers pages, with some financial aid.

kenyon-review-young-writers-winter-onlin.about:
The Kenyon Review, one of America's best-known literary magazines, runs Young Writers Workshops for high-school students who love to write. The Winter Online workshop meets online once a week for six weeks; students write new poetry and prose, share work in small workshops led by published writers, and learn to read like writers.

The 2027 winter workshop runs 23 January–27 February 2027. Applications opened on 26 October 2026 and are due 10 December 2026 (typically a writing sample and short statement). The workshops welcome talented high-school students from around the world; check the time of the weekly session against your time zone.
highlights: Led by writers from a major US literary magazine
Weekly online workshops: no travel needed
Students from around the world
kenyon-review-young-writers-winter-onlin.eligibility: High-school students from any country who write in English.
how_to_apply: Prepare a short writing sample (poetry or prose)
Submit the online application by 10 December 2026
Pay tuition once accepted (aid may be available)
Join the weekly online sessions from 23 January 2027
kenyon-review-young-writers-winter-onlin.costs: Paid workshop; tuition and any financial aid listed on the Kenyon Review Young Writers pages.

korea-university-international-winter-ca.about:
Korea University International Winter Campus (IWC) brings international students to one of Korea's top universities in Seoul over the winter break. The 3-week programme runs 22 December 2026 – 8 January 2027 and the 4-week programme to 18 January 2027.

Courses are taught in English across Korean studies, business, social sciences and Korean language, and two new graduate-level courses were added this year. Cultural activities and field trips complement classes.

Applications close on 6 November 2026, with final tuition payment by 13 November. Note that on-campus housing is already full, so plan off-campus accommodation.
highlights: English-taught courses at a top Korean university
3- or 4-week options
New graduate-level courses
korea-university-international-winter-ca.eligibility: University students worldwide (see How to Apply page for documents).
how_to_apply: Choose the 3- or 4-week programme and courses.
Apply on the KU application portal by 6 November 2026.
Pay tuition by 13 November 2026.
Arrange accommodation (dorms are full).
korea-university-international-winter-ca.costs: Fees on the IWC Fees & Payment page; see the Financial Benefits page for discounts. Housing not available on campus this cycle.

ku-leuven-europe-inside-out-2027.about:
Europe Inside Out is KU Leuven's EU-focused summer school, run jointly by its Faculties of Economics & Business, Arts and Social Sciences. Starting 21 June 2027, students study for two weeks (to 2 July, 6 ECTS) or three weeks (to 9 July, 8 ECTS), with lectures on Doing Business with Europe(ans), Policies & Politics in the EU, Entrepreneurship and Innovation in Europe and Social & Cultural Interactions, a group project presented on the final day, and day trips to Brussels, Antwerp and Paris included in the fee.

It targets graduate students in arts, economics and business, law or social sciences, and final-year undergraduates; participants must be over 18 with at least two years of higher education. Non-European students must register by 1 April 2027.
highlights: EU business, policy and culture at Belgium's oldest university
Day trips to Brussels, Antwerp and Paris included
6 or 8 ECTS with a group project
ku-leuven-europe-inside-out-2027.eligibility: Over 18 with at least two years in higher education: graduate students in arts, economics/business, law or social sciences, or final-year undergraduates (others need some exposure to these fields). All nationalities.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 flyer and provisional programme
Register online and select the applicable fee (partner or non-partner institution)
Pay within 14 days of registering
Non-European students: register by 1 April 2027 and arrange a Schengen visa and accommodation
ku-leuven-europe-inside-out-2027.costs: Registration fee (2027 page): two weeks EUR 600 (partner institutions) or EUR 1,000 (others); three weeks EUR 750 or EUR 1,150. Includes the programme and day trips; travel and accommodation not included.

latvia-state-scholarships-summer-schools.about:
Each year Latvia's State Education Development Agency (VIAA) awards state scholarships for participation in summer schools run by Latvian higher education institutions, under bilateral education agreements. VIAA publishes a list of eligible summer schools (Latvian language and culture courses as well as subject-specific schools) and pays EUR 1,000 per participant directly to the organiser for the duration of the school.

Citizens of agreement countries can apply, and Georgia, Azerbaijan and Ukraine are explicitly listed among them. Only students and academic or research staff of foreign higher education institutions are eligible. Applications and documents go directly to the summer school organiser, and VIAA's committee makes the final decision; participants pay their own travel.
highlights: EUR 1,000 scholarship paid to the summer school
Choose from VIAA's list of Latvian university summer schools
Georgia is an eligible country under a bilateral agreement
latvia-state-scholarships-summer-schools.eligibility: Students and academic/research staff of foreign higher education institutions who are citizens of countries with an education agreement with Latvia (including Georgia, Azerbaijan and Ukraine) or that offer reciprocal scholarships. Qatar is not listed.
how_to_apply: Check VIAA's summer schools page and the list of 2027 summer schools when the call opens (around 1 February 2027)
Choose a summer school and read its application instructions
Send the summer school application form and required documents directly to the Latvian organiser by the deadline (1 April in 2026)
Wait for the organiser to inform you of VIAA's decision
latvia-state-scholarships-summer-schools.costs: Scholarship EUR 1,000 per person for the whole summer school, transferred to the organiser (no cash to the student). Travel to Latvia is self-funded.

leiden-frontiers-childrens-rights-2027.about:
Frontiers of Children's Rights is Leiden Law School's annual summer school taking a close look at contemporary children's rights issues from a legal perspective, with input from other disciplines, legal systems and local perspectives. The 13th edition runs 28 June to 2 July 2027 in Leiden and The Hague.

It is designed for professionals, academics and law students who have completed at least three years of a law degree; applicants from other relevant disciplines may be considered. The group is small (maximum 40), which makes it very interactive.

Applications open on 1 December 2026 and close on 30 April 2027. The theme and fee will be announced on the official page.
highlights: Small group of max. 40
Leiden Law School's children's rights experts
Mix of academics, students and practitioners
leiden-frontiers-childrens-rights-2027.eligibility: Law students with at least three completed years, legal professionals and academics; other relevant disciplines considered. Any nationality.
how_to_apply: Check the official page for the 2027 theme.
Apply from 1 December 2026.
Submit before 30 April 2027.
Contact n.r.s.dole@law.leidenuniv.nl with questions.
leiden-frontiers-childrens-rights-2027.costs: Fee to be confirmed for 2027. Travel and accommodation not included.

leiden-international-criminal-law-summer.about:
Run by Leiden University's Grotius Centre in The Hague, the 'city of international justice', this summer school covers the core crimes (genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, aggression), complementarity, modes of liability, the rights of the accused and the role of victims. Lectures are combined with practical exercises.

The 2027 edition starts on 8 July 2027 and lasts 10 learning days. Participants visit institutions such as the International Criminal Court and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers. The group is capped at 70 participants.

It suits law students who have completed at least one year of a law degree, recent graduates and legal professionals who want a career in international justice.
highlights: Visits to the ICC and Kosovo Specialist Chambers
Taught in The Hague by practitioners and academics
Max. 70 participants
leiden-international-criminal-law-summer.eligibility: Law students with at least one completed year of study, young law graduates and legal professionals; any nationality; English proficiency.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page.
Register online when registration opens in February 2027.
Submit the application before 1 May 2027.
Pay the fee after acceptance.
leiden-international-criminal-law-summer.costs: Tuition €1,550; travel and accommodation not included. No scholarships listed.
